# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-18

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — clear one-liner, the 47+28=76 example, and
`pip install carnot-ebm` up top tell me what this is and how to get it in five
seconds. But the moment I look closer it falls apart: the headline stat block is
contaminated with retro-speak ("Repinned from v2 0.9857"), the Results section
is a wall of undefined benchmark acronyms with several suspiciously perfect /
physically-weird numbers, and the license literally contradicts itself (MIT-0 at
the top, Apache 2.0 at the bottom). A casual visitor keeps scrolling on the
hero's strength; a technical evaluator starts doubting the rigor and the
licensing — which is exactly the person you want to convert.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradiction — hero badge + `<meta>` say "MIT-0", footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License". An adopter cannot tell what they're allowed to do.
2. The "Recent progress" card is wedged inside the above-the-fold stats bar and
   reads like an internal changelog ("Repinned from v2 0.9857", "5-seed
   dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947") — the first thing that breaks
   the stranger's trust, in the most prominent slot on the page.
3. The Results grid is 12 cards of insider jargon (FoVer, CCTU, CRANE, VeriCoT,
   SVAMP, HalluGuard, PRM-BiasBench) plus numbers that invite suspicion — a
   "0.125 FoVer baseline" (below random!), "60/60", "0.5 → 1.0", "2.0× exact".

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- No hard word-count violations: every bento card body is < 120 words, the
  "Recent progress" r-card is ~47 words (< 60 cap), and the results-grid has 12
  cards (< 20 cap). Bloat is NOT the page's problem — density and jargon are.
- Caveat: the Results section packs 12 dense, acronym-heavy cards back-to-back.
  A stranger skims none of them. Effective bloat-by-density even though each card
  is individually short — consider trimming to the strongest ~6.
- Nav has 11 link items + 2 buttons (13 targets). Borderline cluttered; not fatal.

### Internal jargon
- Hero stats bar / "Recent progress" card (line 308–312) — "FoVer", "5-seed",
  "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857"
  — a stranger has no idea what FoVer is, what "repinned" means, or why there are
  three different AUROC numbers (0.9131 / 0.8947 / 0.9857) in two sentences.
- Features → "Typed constraints" (451) — "CCTU constrained tool-use
  micro-benchmark". CCTU never defined.
- Features → "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" (497–499) — the single most opaque
  card on the page: "scales Test-Time Compute (TTC) based on Process-Reward
  Energy Model (PREM) variance ... intrinsic motivation for continuous
  self-learning." Pure research-speak; zero stated user benefit.
- Results cards (548–576) — "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC", "CRANE vs rigid
  grammar", "VeriCoT equation-style CoT fix", "GSM8K extraction TP rate",
  "PRM-BiasBench-style attacks", "k=5 ensemble", "HalluGuard v3". A stranger
  knows none of SVAMP / CRANE / VeriCoT / CoT / GSM8K / TP / PRM / k=5.
- Preprint (584–594) — "paper-v6", "non-operator environment",
  "operator-initiated upload". "operator" and "paper-v6" are internal terms.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Stats bar (306) — "382 Completed milestones" as a headline number. Milestone
  count is an internal process metric; a stranger doesn't know what a "milestone"
  is here and can't value it. Same concern for "3,761 Experiment runs" (305) —
  reads as internal activity volume, not user benefit.
- "Recent progress" card (312) — "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission
  adversarial audit" is a retrospective/changelog sentence, not landing-page copy.

### Inconsistencies
- License: "MIT-0 · Open Source" (hero badge, line 291) and `<meta>` "MIT-0"
  (line 7) vs footer "Apache 2.0 License" (line 766). Direct contradiction.
- AUROC sprawl: 0.9131 (hero stat, 308), 0.8947 ("architecture-only", 312),
  0.9857 ("v2", retracted, 312), 0.91 ("publication gate", 530), 0.90 AUC (550).
  Five numbers; a stranger can't tell which is "the" result.
- "FoVer" appears as both a strong result (0.9131 AUROC, 308) and a near-broken
  baseline (0.125 AUC, 550). Same name, wildly different numbers, no explanation
  that these are different tasks (verifier-ensemble-on-FoVer vs
  EstimationVerifier-on-SVAMP). Looks self-contradictory at a glance.
- Section says "Seven capabilities" / "What you can check" (415–416), but of the
  7 bento cards, 3 are not user-facing checks: "Research operations" (dev loop),
  "APIs & portable memory" (integration surfaces), "TTC & PREM" (internal
  controller). The framing oversells "things you can verify."

### Missing essentials
- A single, consistent LICENSE statement (see contradiction above).
- Sample sizes / denominators on most result cards. "60/60", "TP 0.5 → 1.0",
  "+4.9 points" have no N — the page claims artifacts back every number but
  doesn't show or link them per-card, so I can't actually check the trust claim.
- Definitions/links for the benchmark names. "Every number is backed by an
  artifact" (511) but no card links to its artifact.
- Maintainer signal is thin — footer "Ian Blenke · Carnot Project" is the only
  human anchor; fine, but combined with "autonomous research loop" a stranger may
  wonder if anyone is actually steering it.

### Fabrication signals
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" (550) — an AUC of 0.125 is far BELOW
  random (0.5). A baseline that wrong reads as a sign error or a cherry-picked
  framing; "we beat a catastrophically broken baseline" is not a credible flex.
  Biggest red flag on the page for anyone who knows ROC.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (565) — perfect 100% on N=60, no FPR.
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (560) — perfect 1.0, no N.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (540) — exactly-2.0× ideal linear scaling on
  two GPUs is suspiciously clean.
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" (431) — very high, though at least anchored to
  the stated 164-problem HumanEval set (the one number that shows its work).
- "0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings" (570) — a null result (changed
  nothing) dressed as a headline evidence card.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: jargon-free one-sentence value prop, a concrete
  47+28=76 example, "second pair of eyes" framing, and `pip install carnot-ebm`
  + HuggingFace mirror visible immediately. A stranger understands the product.
- "How it works → Extract → Check → Repair" (351–409) is genuinely good plain

- The provenance/honesty posture is a real asset: "labeled by provenance"
  (513), the two-AUROCs blog, and the Preprint's independent-reproduction note
  (589–593). The problem is the jargon, not the integrity.
